episodes.name: episode 3
episodes.material: tenor and alto imitate final figure of answer; bass falling sequence from soprano figure of bar 15 and chromatic CS steps; after cadence in III at 25 soprano and alto imitate final figure of subject

episodes.name: episode 4
episodes.material: final figure of subject in bass; soprano alludes to detached crotchets of bar 13; alto part of CS

episodes.name: episode 5
episodes.material: new development of final subject figure, alto imitated by soprano; ornamental figure later used by bass

episodes.name: episode 6
episodes.material: final figure of inverted subject; soprano and bass in tenths imitated by alto and tenor in tenths

episodes.name: episode 7

countersubjects.notes: introduces an almost complete rising chromatic scale; its quaver figure anticipates by inversion the answer's final figure; inverted CS used with inverted subject

subject.ends: on the mediant (d-flat), answered with tierce de Picardie (a-natural)
subject.answer: real; of the ten minor-key fugues whose subjects end on the mediant only I.10 also uses tierce de Picardie for the first answer

claims.claim: Only I.10 among ten minor fugues with mediant-ending subjects also uses tierce de Picardie in the first answer
Countersubject introduces an almost complete rising chromatic scale
Stretti are at one beat's distance, at seventh/ninth (direct and inverted) and sixth (direct vs inverted)
Stretto 4 is effectively the final section; apparent tierce de Picardie in alto bar 97 is a doubled leading-note to the subdominant chord
The ear hardly notices that the lower voices omit the final figures of the subject in the climax
